Senses.Explanation: In Chan questions, instructions, and verdicts, the headword names a person's footing—the standing-ground directly under the heels. Masters ask what is there, tell people to plant it firmly, or say it does not touch the ground, making an anatomical image into a public test of where someone stands. Poshan Haiming gives the stock verdict “right under the heel, worth thirty blows” (腳跟下好與三十棒), and Chaozong Tongren says that something shines through past and present under the assembled people's heels (諸公腳跟下有一段輝騰今古). Doushuai Bulin Jian asks what the matter under one's heels is (腳跟下事作麼生) and then tells his attendant to bring the sandals. Yangzhuo Zhengming tells an interlocutor that his heels do not touch the ground (闍黎腳跟不點地), while Poshan says that one who travels and resides in the world must first plant the heels firmly and not be stirred by the eight winds (行腳住世先要立定腳跟，不被八風所鼓). Linquan Conglun preserves the graphic variant in a verdict that the heels do not touch the ground (脚跟不點地). These uses are distinct from bodily injury to the heel.
Senses.Note: The headword has 1,607 hits in 211 allowlisted texts; the graphic variant (脚跟) has 1,288 hits in 132. The matter under the heels (腳跟下事) occurs 60 times in 39 texts, planting the heels firmly (立定腳跟) 24 times in 18, and heels not touching ground (腳跟不點地) 21 times in 17. Five exact headword witnesses and two marked graphic-variant witnesses cover locative, stance, question, instruction, and verdict deployments.

Senses.Explanation: In injury descriptions, the headword names the anatomical heel: it bleeds or is struck by an axe. Those bodily predicates keep this referent separate from the footing tested in Chan exchanges. Konggu Daocheng predicates bleeding of it in the line “split open the skull; the heel runs blood” (打開腦蓋，腳跟流血). Fushi Yigong's lineage verse says that the heel was suddenly injured by an axe (腳跟忽被斧頭傷). No special Chan loading is asserted for this ordinary anatomical sense.
Senses.Note: Two independent records anchor bodily predicates. No special Zen deviation is asserted for this ordinary anatomical sense. A superficially anatomical stock beating formula was excluded after its grammar was checked; the exclusion and its reason remain recorded in WORK.md.
